title: How to call a waiter in Korea: 여기요! 🙋 #learnkorean
caption:
In a Korean restaurant, you usually call the server yourself. One word does it:

여기요! (yeo-gi-yo) = Over here, please!
여기 (yeo-gi) = here
요 (yo) = the polite ending

저기요 (jeo-gi-yo) works too, and many tables have a call button. 여기요 only calls the server, so you still order after that 😄

pinnedComment: What do you say to call a waiter in your country? 👇
alt: A busy needle-felted Korean barbecue restaurant. Everyone eats except a coral felt mascot with an empty cup. A server runs past. It whispers 저… 저기… and another server rushes by. It tries 안녕하세요 and a server only bows back and leaves. At the next table an auntie shouts 여기요! and three servers run to her. The mascot breathes in until its body swells, the room goes silent, and it shouts 여기요! Three servers turn at once and run over. 여기 means here and 요 is the polite ending. Delighted, it keeps shouting until it is buried under a mountain of food with only its eyes showing. It whispers 여기요 and the servers run back: 네! 또 뭐 드릴까요? (Anything else?)
